rows: Seek/interpret evidence consistent with existing belief
Debug by testing only expected behavior paths
Weight prior irrecoverable costs in future decisions
Keep rewriting bad code because "we've already spent 3 months"
Underestimate time/cost of future projects; ignore outside view
Confidence exceeds accuracy; 90% CI intervals too narrow
"I knew it all along" after the fact
Post-mortems: "Of course the system would fail that way"
Prefer current state; change requires extra justification
Unskilled overestimate competence; experts underestimate (often misrepresented: the original paper showed both, replication contested)
Why vivid examples dominate probability estimates
Use base rates and outside view; availability helps only when memory frequency tracks world frequency.
Why a category match overrides statistics
Force base-rate computation before judging similarity.
Why the first number contaminates estimates
Generate an independent estimate before seeing anchors or negotiate from multiple anchors.
Reframe the same options both ways and check whether preference changes.
Why teams seek only supporting evidence
Use pre-mortems, adversarial collaboration, or red-team review.
Why project estimates are too optimistic
Why irrecoverable costs keep driving decisions
Ask whether you would start the project today with no prior spend.
Reframe as opportunity cost and compute expected value explicitly.
